name: Tawa Pulao

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ tsp plus a pinch in the rice water; ¼ tsp on the tawa

equipment: Tawa (large flat griddle) or a wide, heavy pan: the dish's namesake; the wide surface lets the rice fry and pick up a little smoky edge
Saucepan for the rice and a small pan for the vegetables
Sieve or colander to rinse and drain the rice
Wide plate for cooling the rice, chopping board, knife, kitchen scale, measuring spoons
Flat steel spatula or a wide spoon (the back of it is used to mash the tomato and vegetables)

steps.title: Measure and rinse the rice
steps.text: Put 70 g basmati in a bowl. Cover with cold water, swirl with your fingers, tip out the cloudy water, and repeat 3 times.
steps.visualCue: The water turns from milky to nearly clear on the third rinse
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl of rinsed rice with nearly clear water
steps.videoShot: Water swirling cloudy to clear over the rice.
steps.watchOut: Rubbing the grains hard, which breaks them and makes the rice sticky; swirl gently.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Cover the rice with water again and leave it for 20 min. Do steps 5 to 9 meanwhile.
steps.visualCue: The grains turn from translucent to opaque white and look a little longer
steps.videoShot: Rice sitting in water, grains turning white.
steps.watchOut: Soaking much longer than 30 min, which makes the grains fragile and mushy; if you forgot, just rinse and cook for 1 minute less.

steps.title: Boil the rice
steps.text: Bring 350 ml water and a pinch of salt (1 g) to a rolling boil in a saucepan. Drain the soaked rice, add it, and boil uncovered on medium for 8–9 min.
steps.visualCue: Grains swell to about double their length and a grain pressed between two fingers is soft outside with a tiny firm dot in the centre
steps.cameraCheck: A grain of rice pressed between two fingers
steps.watchOut: Cooking until fully soft, which turns into a clump in the pan later (it keeps cooking when tossed); drain while there is still a slight bite. If it overcooks, spread it thin and let it dry longer in step 4.

steps.title: Drain and cool the rice
steps.text: Drain through the sieve, shake off the water, and spread the rice on a wide plate. Fluff it with a fork and leave it for 10 min.
steps.tip: Leftover cooked rice from the fridge, about 210 g, works even better; skip steps 1 to 4 and break up the lumps with your fingers.
steps.visualCue: Grains look dry on the surface and separate when you tilt the plate
steps.cameraCheck: The plate of fluffy, separate rice
steps.videoShot: Fork fluffing steaming rice on a plate.
steps.watchOut: Leaving the rice heaped and damp, which makes it clump and turn mushy on the tawa; spread it wider and fan it if it stays wet.

steps.title: Dice the potato and carrot
steps.text: Cut 30 g potato and 20 g carrot into 1 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: Even small cubes, all about the size of a green pea cluster
steps.watchOut: Cubes of mixed sizes, so small ones turn to mush while big ones stay hard; re-cut any large piece to match.

steps.title: Boil the potato and carrot
steps.text: Put the cubes in a small pan with 150 ml water and a tiny pinch of salt. Bring to a boil and cook 5 min.
steps.visualCue: A fork slides into a potato cube with slight resistance
steps.cameraCheck: A fork piercing a potato cube
steps.watchOut: Boiling until the potato falls apart, since it will be pressed again on the tawa; test at 4 min.

steps.title: Add the peas
steps.text: Add 25 g green peas to the same pan and boil 3 min more. Drain all the vegetables and keep them aside.
steps.visualCue: Peas turn bright green and slightly wrinkle when pressed
steps.cameraCheck: The drained vegetables in the sieve
steps.videoShot: Water draining from the colourful vegetables.
steps.watchOut: Pale, dull peas from overboiling; drain at once and the colour holds.

steps.title: Chop the onion, tomato and capsicum
steps.text: Chop 30 g onion and 50 g tomato fine, and cut 25 g capsicum into small pieces about 5 mm.
steps.visualCue: Three small piles of similar-sized pieces: white-purple onion, red tomato, green capsicum
steps.cameraCheck: The three piles on the board
steps.watchOut: Big capsicum chunks that stay raw while the rice is done; cut small so everything is the same size as a pea.

steps.title: Prep the aromatics
steps.text: Grate 2 g ginger and 2 g garlic, slit or chop 1 green chilli (3 g), and chop 3 g coriander leaves. Measure out 4 g pav bhaji masala, 1 g red chilli powder and 0.5 g turmeric in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: A small wet pile of ginger and garlic, and a bowl of dark red-brown powder
steps.cameraCheck: The small bowl of measured spices
steps.videoShot: Spoon dropping masala into a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Measuring the powders only after the pan is hot; they take seconds to burn, so have them ready in the bowl first.

steps.title: Heat the tawa and the fat
steps.text: Put the tawa or wide pan on medium-high for 1 min. Add 3 g (¾ tsp) oil, then 8 g (2 tsp) butter, and let the butter melt.
steps.visualCue: The butter melts and foams gently, smelling nutty and sweet, without turning brown
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with melted, foaming butter
steps.videoShot: Butter melting and foaming in the oil.
steps.watchOut: Butter that browns or smokes, since it tastes bitter; the oil protects it, but if it browns, lower the heat and wipe out and restart.
steps.funFact: Street vendors make tawa pulao on the same big tawa used for pav bhaji, which is where the name comes from (Tarla Dalal; Chitra's Food Book).

steps.title: Add the cumin
steps.text: Lower to medium, add 1 g cumin seeds and stir for 10 sec.
steps.visualCue: Seeds sizzle and darken slightly, and the smell is warm and toasty
steps.cameraCheck: The cumin sizzling in the pan
steps.watchOut: Black, burnt cumin; if it turns black, start again, as it will taste bitter.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add 30 g chopped onion and stir for 3 min on medium until soft.
steps.visualCue: Onion turns translucent and just starts to turn pale gold, and smells sweet
steps.watchOut: Dark brown onion edges, which make the pulao taste heavy and burnt; add 1 tbsp water and lower the heat if they colour too fast.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Add the grated ginger and garlic and the green chilli, and stir for 30 sec.
steps.visualCue: The raw sharp smell turns warm and savoury
steps.watchOut: Garlic that browns and turns bitter; keep stirring and move straight on to the capsicum.

steps.title: Cook the capsicum
steps.text: Add 25 g capsicum and stir for 2 min.
steps.visualCue: Pieces turn a slightly deeper green and shiny but still have bite
steps.watchOut: Cooking until the capsicum is soft and olive-coloured; it should keep some crunch, so move on at 2 min.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add 50 g chopped tomato and 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt. Cook 3–4 min, pressing with the back of the spoon, until pulpy.
steps.visualCue: The tomato melts into a thick, jammy paste and a little butter shows at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The pulpy tomato masala in the pan
steps.watchOut: Tomato still in chunks and sour; keep pressing and cooking until no raw pieces remain.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the heat. Add the pav bhaji masala, red chilli powder and turmeric with 1 tbsp water, and stir for 30 sec.
steps.visualCue: The masala turns a deep brick red and smells strongly toasty and spicy
steps.cameraCheck: The red masala in the pan
steps.watchOut: Powders that stick and burn on a dry pan, with a sharp acrid smell; the splash of water prevents it, and if they stick, add another tablespoon of water at once.

steps.title: Add the boiled vegetables
steps.text: Add the drained potato, carrot and peas. Press and mix with the back of the spoon for 2 min, mashing a few pieces lightly.
steps.visualCue: The vegetables are coated deep red and a few cubes are crushed into the masala
steps.cameraCheck: The coated vegetables in the pan
steps.videoShot: Spoon pressing vegetables into the red masala.
steps.watchOut: A watery pan from wet vegetables; if there is water, cook 1 more minute until the masala clings to the vegetables.

steps.title: Add the rice and toss
steps.text: Add the cooled rice. Fold and toss gently on medium for 3 min, with a light pressing motion, until every grain is coloured.
steps.visualCue: Grains are evenly reddish-orange with no white streaks and the rice is hot and fragrant
steps.cameraCheck: The tossed pulao showing even colour
steps.videoShot: Spatula folding red masala into the rice.
steps.watchOut: Stirring hard, which breaks the grains and makes the pulao pasty; lift and fold instead, and if white patches remain, toss 1 more minute.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Add 5 ml (1 tsp) lemon juice and 3 g coriander, fold once, taste and add a pinch of salt only if needed. Rest 1 min.
steps.visualCue: A glossy, reddish-orange, separate-grained pulao with a fresh lemon and coriander smell
steps.cameraCheck: The finished pulao on a plate
steps.videoShot: Coriander and lemon dropping onto the pulao.
steps.watchOut: Adding lemon on very high heat, which dulls its freshness; add it after switching off. If the rice is dry, add 1 tsp butter and fold.

reasons: about 150 g of vegetables with only 8 g butter and 3 g oil, no frying of the rice and no added sugar, plus a good vitamin C and vitamin A from the capsicum, tomato and carrot. Points off for being mostly white rice (about 55 g carbs from rice, low protein of about 9 g and only about 5.5 g fibre), and for sodium of about 800 mg (40% of a daily limit). Street and restaurant versions typically use 2 to 4 tbsp butter or oil per plate and more salt and masala, with a larger rice portion, often 500 kcal or more (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very widely published Mumbai street-food rice, found on Veg Recipes of India, Hebbar's Kitchen, Swasthi's Indian Healthy Recipes, Chitra's Food Book, Cook With Manali, Tarla Dalal, Sanjeev Kapoor and many others, usually called a quick, spicy, tangy, loved lunchbox and leftover-rice meal. Points off because it is a simple variation on fried rice that depends heavily on the brand of pav bhaji masala, and the tawa smokiness is hard to recreate at home. Recipe-site star counts were not checked this run. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 1 day (cool within 1 hour; cooked rice should not stay warm for long). Freezing is not recommended: the vegetables turn soft and the rice turns grainy. Reheat in a pan on medium with 1–2 tsp water, tossing for 2–3 min until steaming hot all through.
leftoverRemix: Tawa pulao cutlets or stuffed paratha. Mash the cold leftover pulao with 1 boiled potato and 1 tbsp breadcrumbs or besan, shape into flat patties, and shallow-fry in ½ tsp oil on the tawa until crisp; or stuff the mash into atta dough for a spicy paratha.
burnOff: about 6.1 km of running (430 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.6 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 43 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With raita (about 490 kcal): about 7 km running or 9.8 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: rice, onion, garlic, table salt and pav bhaji masala are all out under the common rule set (assumption: the common rule set; families differ).

ekadashi.reason: rice is a grain avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set, and onion and garlic are avoided too.

jain.reason: onion, garlic, fresh ginger, potato and carrot are roots; cook the Jain variant.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; fine as a one-pot iftar dinner, but moderately salty (about 800 mg sodium) and butter-rich for sehri.

jain.reason: the main recipe uses onion, garlic, fresh ginger, potato and carrot; cook the Jain variant (no onion, garlic, ginger, potato or carrot, with sonth and a Jain pav bhaji masala).

vegan.reason: butter 8 g is dairy; use the Vegan variant (oil or vegan butter instead).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, so no meat or egg; no fish needed.

sattvik.reason: the main recipe uses onion 30 g and garlic 2 g; skip both and use a no-onion no-garlic pav bhaji masala (Not researched yet as a separate variant; the Jain variant already drops both).

glutenFree.reason: rice and vegetables only, no wheat, rava, maida or hing in the recipe. Check the pav bhaji masala label (blend contents were not checked this run); most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so use none or gluten-free hing.

dairyFree.reason: butter 8 g is dairy; swap for oil (see the Dairy-free and Vegan variant).
